subject: organ transplant cooler
title: The 5 Organs That Last Longest on Ice, Ranked (#1 Waits 36 Hours)

scenes.text: One organ can wait a day and a half on ice. The heart isn't even close.
Number five: the heart. On ice, it has only four to six hours to beat again.
scenes.label: Heart · 4-6 hours

scenes.text: Number four: the lungs. Four to eight hours, so they often travel by plane.
scenes.label: Lungs · 4-8 hours

scenes.text: Number three: the liver. Eight to twelve hours for the body's biggest internal organ.
scenes.label: Liver · 8-12 hours

scenes.text: Number two: the pancreas. Twelve to eighteen hours packed in cold solution.
scenes.label: Pancreas · 12-18 hours

scenes.text: Number one: the kidney. Twenty-four to thirty-six hours, a day and a half on ice.
scenes.label: Kidney · 24-36 hours

description:
How long donated organs can be kept on ice before transplant, according to the windows used by US organ procurement organizations: heart 4-6 hours, lungs 4-8 hours, liver 8-12 hours, pancreas 12-18 hours, kidney 24-36 hours.
The intestines (8-16 hours) overlap the liver, and newer perfusion machines that pump fluid through an organ can stretch these times.
Why do you think the kidney can wait so much longer than the heart?
first_comment: Which organ would you have put at number one? And what should we rank next in the human body?
